newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sees small Q2 surplus, plans new debt issues.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees small Q2 surplus, plans new debt issues.

text.p: Mexico will likely scratch out a small fiscal surplus in the second quarter, but this will move into deficit in the year's second half as pension reforms kick in, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Monday.

He said Mexico was planning to launch more longer-term debt on the domestic market to help finance that deficit, fuelled by the government's continued payment of state pensions while the majority of workers move into new private pension funds.

"We had a surplus in the first quarter and it is probable we will have a small surplus in the second, but then the deficit will increase in the second half, because that is when the pension reform begins," he said in an interview on the fringes of an international insurance conference here.

He said the government planned to finance the increasing deficit, which he said would reach 0.5 percent of gross domestic product for the year, by stepping up longer term domestic debt issues in the coming weeks.

"In order for us to have this deficit of around half a (percentage) point of GDP for the year, this will be financed mainly by increased issuance of long-term bonds in the internal market -- above all Udibonos and Bondes," he said.
"Long-term issues of three to five years that give a return above the level of inflation have been in strong demand and there could be an increase in these bonds in the coming weeks," he added.
Udibonos are inflation-linked debt instruments while Bondes are straight debt issues. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
